Findings.Comment: Returning here keeps the panel open after the trigger has already blurred: `relatedTarget === null` means focus went to `document.body`, which is outside `element.nativeElement`, so from that point on no `focusout` bubbles through the panel host. Realistic path on a narrow screen (phone or a desktop window under 600px): open the panel, tap the non-focusable help text — the trigger blurs and this guard swallows the resulting `focusout` — then tap or tab to any control outside the panel. The element losing focus is now `body` or that outside control, `onFocusOut` never runs, and the panel stays open with keyboard focus elsewhere, breaking the "close the panel when focus leaves it" behaviour after the first such tap. The only escape is finding the toggle again.

Findings.Comment: The `pointerInteractionInside` flag is reset by `document:pointerup`, but on touch input the blur that produces this `focusout` is triggered by the compatibility `mousedown`, which browsers dispatch after `pointerup`. So tapping non-focusable help text inside the panel on a narrow/touch screen reaches `event.relatedTarget === null` with the flag already `false`, and `isOpen` is set to `false` — the exact case the comment above the guard says the flag guards. Mouse input works, because blur happens at `mousedown`, before `pointerup`; the guard only applies at `max-width: 599px`, i.e. precisely where touch is the norm.

Findings.Comment: `loyalty_discount` computes `percent = min(Decimal(years) * Decimal(2), Decimal(10))`, which clamps only the upper bound. If the caller passes a negative `years` value (a stale or malformed loyalty record from the backend, or an uninitialized default), `percent` is negative, `min` keeps it, and `apply_percentage` computes `(100 - percent) / 100` > 1, so the returned "discounted" amount is larger than the input amount. The function then silently raises the price instead of applying no discount. Clamping the lower bound at zero makes the intent explicit and keeps the result a reduction for any integer input.

PreExisting.Headline: Get-leave failure in onReportReturnClick is an unhandled rejection
PreExisting.Explanation: The async click handler awaits `leaveApi.getLeave` with no try/catch and the template event binding does not observe the returned promise, so any network or API error surfaces as an unhandled rejection and the CTA silently does nothing. The `claimNumber ?? ''` fallback compounds this: when `claim()` has no claim number the request goes to `/api/claims//leave`, which fails and takes the same silent path.

Findings.Comment: On touch input the compatibility `mousedown` that moves focus (and thus fires this `focusout`) is dispatched *after* `pointerup`, so `onPointerUp()` has already reset `pointerInteractionInside` to false by the time the guard runs. On a tablet or touch laptop with a viewport of 600px or more, tapping non-focusable help text inside the panel while the trigger has focus therefore reaches the guard with `relatedTarget === null` and the flag already false, falls through to `isOpen.set(false)`, and dismisses the panel — exactly the case the guard and its comment exist to prevent. Clearing the flag on the gesture's `click` (or after the compatibility mouse events) instead of `pointerup` keeps it set across that blur; `pointercancel` still covers gestures taken over by a scroll.

One of the two is wrong: either the media-query condition is inverted, or the comment describes stale intent. As written, anyone adjusting the breakpoint or the dismissal rules will do so against a false premise.

Findings.Comment: `pointerInteractionInside` is only cleared by `document:pointerup` / `document:pointercancel`. If the pointer is released outside the document (mouse dragged past the window edge and released, or released over browser chrome), neither event reaches the document and the flag stays `true` indefinitely. The next `focusout` with `relatedTarget === null` — e.g. clicking a non-focusable background area outside the panel — then hits the `event.relatedTarget === null && this.pointerInteractionInside` guard and the panel fails to dismiss once, until some later `pointerup` in the document clears the flag. Only occurs after a gesture that ends outside the page.

Findings.Comment: `invoice.getPayments().get(0)` assumes a PAID invoice always has at least one `Payment`, but this very class violates that: `markPaidExternally` sets the status to `PAID` while explicitly recording no `Payment` (its javadoc says so). Calling `receiptFor` on such an invoice throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 0 out of bounds for length 0` instead of producing a receipt. An empty payments list (or a null list, depending on how the entity is loaded) makes every receipt request for externally settled invoices crash. The pick-`get(0)` choice is also fragile when an invoice has several payments, since nothing guarantees which element is first. Prefer a guarded lookup that falls back to the invoice-level timestamp/method when no `Payment` exists, or pick the latest payment explicitly.

For any invoice paid outside the platform, `invoice.getPayments()` is empty, so `get(0)` throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of returning a receipt for an invoice that is legitimately PAID. Previously the receipt was built from `invoice.getUpdatedAt()`, which worked for both payment paths; the added call only holds for invoices with at least one recorded `Payment`. A second, related edge: an invoice settled by several partial payments takes `get(0)`, whose date and method are not necessarily the settling transaction's.
